notes: Short summary: Large industrial automation vendor evaluating Redwood Dedicated for multi-site chat/code-assistant and low-latency reranking across global control centers. Primary ask: reserved capacity with deterministic throughput and priority lanes to protect latency-sensitive routes. Interested in traffic shaping (per-route quotas, token-based priority lanes), tenant isolation guarantees, noisy-neighbor mitigation (CPU/GPU QoS + scheduling), and clear SLOs/SLA credit policy. Procurement wants predictable cost via reserved GPUs and a defined upgrade path for bursts. Security: VPC-only control plane, enterprise KMS, SOC2, SSO integration, EU data residency for EU plants. AE notes: customer repeatedly asked "How do you guarantee p95 for critical routes during large batch jobs?". SE note: request for microbench (8-H100 pool simulation) + network isolation test. Legal: pushing for 99.95% uptime and extended credits for degradation longer than 30m.
